reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: Combines early-onset immune dysregulation with immunodeficiency, typically presenting in childhood with severe autoimmunity, enteropathy, lymphoproliferation and recurrent infection
Autoimmune cytopenias, chronic diarrhoea with an inflammatory bowel disease-like enteropathy and endocrinopathies such as type 1 diabetes and thyroid disease are common
Hypogammaglobulinaemia with poor vaccine responses frequently develops, so cases are often initially labelled common variable immunodeficiency
The mechanism converges on CTLA-4, because LRBA loss accelerates CTLA-4 degradation, so the phenotype closely resembles CTLA4 haploinsufficiency
Granulomatous-lymphocytic interstitial lung disease and organ-infiltrating lymphocytic disease can occur
Inheritance is autosomal recessive, from biallelic loss-of-function variants in LRBA
CTLA4-Ig fusion therapy (abatacept) is effective because it substitutes for the reduced CTLA-4 signalling, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is curative in severe disease
Diagnosis rests on reduced or absent LRBA protein by flow cytometry together with biallelic variants
reference.pathophysiology: LRBA (lipopolysaccharide-responsive beige-like anchor protein) is an intracellular trafficking protein that protects CTLA-4 from lysosomal degradation and recycles it back to the cell surface. In its absence, CTLA-4 is degraded excessively, so regulatory T cells cannot deliver the inhibitory signal that normally restrains effector T-cell activation. The resulting loss of peripheral tolerance produces widespread autoimmunity and lymphocytic organ infiltration, mirroring CTLA4 haploinsufficiency, while impaired B-cell survival and differentiation lead to progressive hypogammaglobulinaemia and infection susceptibility. Because the defect ultimately reduces functional CTLA-4, replacing that signal is therapeutically effective.
additionalDifferentials: Very-early-onset inflammatory bowel disease of other genetic cause
additionalInvestigations: Flow cytometry for LRBA protein expression in lymphocytes
Lymphocyte subsets and regulatory T-cell enumeration with CTLA-4 expression studies
Serum immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses
Autoantibody screen and direct antiglobulin test for autoimmune cytopenias
LRBA gene sequencing for biallelic loss-of-function variants
Endoscopy with biopsy and chest imaging for enteropathy and interstitial lung disease
redFlags: Severe autoimmune cytopenia with life-threatening anaemia or bleeding
Refractory enteropathy with malnutrition and growth failure
Lymphoproliferation or organomegaly raising concern for malignant transformation
New endocrine crisis such as diabetic ketoacidosis or adrenal insufficiency
reference.prognosis: Untreated disease is severe and often life-limiting from autoimmune and infective complications, but recognition allows targeted CTLA4-Ig therapy and, where indicated, haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, both of which substantially improve outcome.
pitfalls: Settling on a diagnosis of common variable immunodeficiency and not pursuing genetic and protein testing
Treating the enteropathy as ordinary inflammatory bowel disease
Overlooking the shared CTLA-4 mechanism and the resulting response to targeted therapy
Missing associated endocrinopathies until they present in crisis
Delaying definitive treatment until multi-organ autoimmune damage is established
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Use CTLA4-Ig therapy (abatacept) as targeted treatment, replacing the deficient CTLA-4 inhibitory signal to control the immune dysregulation
Give immunoglobulin replacement for hypogammaglobulinaemia and antimicrobial prophylaxis to reduce recurrent infection
Control autoimmunity and lymphoproliferation with immunosuppression, using agents such as sirolimus, corticosteroids or other steroid-sparing drugs as needed
Consider allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation as a potentially curative option in severe disease

Monitor for and treat organ-specific complications including autoimmune cytopenias, enteropathy, endocrinopathies such as type 1 diabetes and thyroid disease, and granulomatous-lymphocytic interstitial lung disease
Coordinate care through clinical immunology alongside relevant organ specialists
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive disorder with cascade family testing
Escalate for severe cytopenias, uncontrolled autoimmunity or progressive lung disease
